articles.title: Chris Pratt Says He ‘Would Love’ James Gunn to Direct a Fourth ‘Guardians of the Galaxy’ Film After DC Exit
articles.summary: Chris Pratt thinks it would be “awesome” to reunite with James Gunn for a fourth “Guardians of the Galaxy” film after the director announced his departure from DC Studios this week. Gunn and his co-chief, Peter Safran, were ousted from their positions on Nov.
body: The executive shuffle marks another setback for DC Studios, which has struggled to compete with the powerhouse that is Disney’s Marvel Cinematic Universe of late. But it opens a route for Gunn to return to the MCU, where he directed three “Guardians of the Galaxy” movies.

Pratt recently told Moviezine that he would love to reunite with Gunn for a fourth film in the franchise. “That would be awesome. I love working with James. He’s the man,” Pratt said when asked about the possibility of making the film. “I haven’t had a chance to speak with him since that news came out yesterday…. It’s always tough because anytime something like this comes up, it could always become a headline.”
He continued: “All I’ll say is I love James. He directed all three movies, and that’s pretty rare… so if he wanted to come back and bring it back, I would love that.”

Pratt has starred as Star-Lord in the franchise across six films, with 2014’s “Guardians of the Galaxy,” “Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2,” “Avengers: Infinity War,” “Avengers: Endgame,” “Thor: Love and Thunder” and most recently in “Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3.”

articles.title: Philippines Wins Inaugural Eurovision Song Contest Asia in Thailand
articles.summary: The Philippines has won the first ever Eurovision Song Contest Asia. Carmelle, representing the Phillippines, scooped first place with the track “Sobra-Sobra,” earning 211 points.
body: The first ever Asian edition of the contest was held Saturday in the Thai capital of Bangkok. Eleven countries took part, including Cambodia, Mongolia and Korea. Like the European edition, which recently celebrated 70 years, points were awarded via a combination of national juries and public vote.
A “rest of the world” vote also awarded a set of points equivalent to that of one participating country, with audiences from 183 countries and territories worldwide having their say.

The contest was aired in the participating countries as well as on Eurovision’s official YouTube channel. EBU members TVP (Poland), Sveriges Radio (Sweden), Kan (Israel) and SBS (Australia) also broadcast the contest, which was hosted by Thai TV stars Woody Milintachinda and Cindy Bishop.

As well as the competing countries, Thai superstar Jeff Satur performed alongside this year’s Eurovision winner Dara, who took first place for Bulgaria in the May contest with her track “Bangaranga.” The show, which also included a special opening performance celebrating the host city, was produced by Voxovation and Bangkok-based S20 Productions. It was sponsored by Zoop.

articles.title: Is ‘Club Kid’ a ‘Conservative’ Movie? Only If You’re Still Living in the ’60s
articles.summary: One of the things I love about movies is how layered they are. When a film connects on a deep level, saying what it’s truly “about” may not be as simple as it sounds. Chasing down a movie’s inner meaning can lead you into the mystery of things. A great movie can be “about” more
body: What “Club Kid” is “about” is how Peter, a charming dissolute man-child, living an existence of unhinged hedonism, discovers that he wants to grow up and take care of someone besides himself. On that score, the drama is authentic and fully felt. In outline, though, it’s something we’ve seen many times before, in films from “About a Boy” to “Big Daddy.” Yet what makes “Club Kid” singular is that it’s about something larger than that.

And yet…he’s not merely celebrating it. Far from it. As authentic and scene-specific as they are, the party sequences in “Club Kid” signify as more than just a portrayal of the New York queer club scene. They’re also a larger snapshot of what party culture, out there in the world, has become: an arena of liberation that’s rooted in a place of physical and spiritual abandon that contains the seeds of destruction.

When a film connects on a deep level, saying what it’s truly “about” may not be as simple as it sounds.

articles.title: ‘I relive that mission every single day of my life’: how Black soldiers handled the Vietnam war
articles.summary: In ambitious documentary Soul Patrol, the complicated experiences of the Vietnam war’s first Black special ops team are explored both on and off the battleground. Ask the average American to name an elite US fighting force, and they might kick off with the Rangers or the Seals.
body: Known as long-range reconnaissance patrols, or LRRPs, these small teams of six to eight soldiers were dropped behind enemy lines to track supply routes and hostile positions, sometimes for days at a time. Stealth was essential. Their job was to identify targets and call in the cavalry, usually in the form of airstrikes, while avoiding direct engagement with enemy forces to preserve their cover.

A melancholy new documentary reckons with the weight of it all. Directed by Harper, Soul Patrol uncovers this hidden chapter of US military history: the story of army team 2/6 of company F, 51st infantry, the Vietnam war’s first Black special operations team – a ragtag bunch of daredevils and dreamers who snuck into the jungle, stared down death and lived to tell a tale that has taken half a century to share in living color. Based on a 2003 war memoir of the same name, the film follows author Ed Emanuel as he assembles the team for a gathering that edges from high school reunion to PTSD group therapy session.
The survivor’s guilt has haunted the team ever since. “I relive that mission every single day of my life,” Emanuel says. “We survived the war, but there was no peace.”

articles.summary: Front-runner Carmelle emerges victorious with her women's empowerment anthem Sobra-Sobra.
body: The Philippines have won the very first Eurovision Song Contest Asia, hosted in Bangkok and with 11 countries vying for the title.
She earned 211 points in total - 93 from the jury and 118 from the public vote - ahead of Thailand's MANG x DAOU in second place with 170 points.
There was a joyous atmosphere at the One Bangkok Arena as the crowd cheered the contestants and celebrated the popular winner.
Carmelle, the youngest contestant in the competition, was an obvious favourite with the juries and the public despite strong showings from several nations.

articles.title: Sotheby's auction of $180m Van Gogh challenged over claims it was 'sold under duress'
articles.summary: Sotheby's says it will work with the heirs of a family who had previously owned the artwork to try and reach a solution.
body: Auction house Sotheby's says it is working to resolve a dispute over the intended sale of a painting by Vincent van Gogh.
Châtaigniers en Fleurs, which carries an estimate of $180m (£136m), is due to go under the hammer in New York on Wednesday.
But representatives acting for heirs of the Fischer family - earlier German owners of the work - say it may have been sold under duress during the rise of the Nazis.
Sotheby's say its own "extensive research" has not established this, but say they will work with the family to try and reach a solution.

articles.title: Noel Fielding 'appalled' by jokes he made with Russell Brand
articles.summary: The Great British Bake Off presenter says he has not been in contact with the convicted rapist "for many years".
body: Noel Fielding has said he is "appalled" by jokes he made alongside Russell Brand when the pair appeared together on TV and at live shows.

The Great British Bake Off presenter said in a statement to the Sun he was "horrified and deeply disturbed" to learn of Brand's crimes, after the disgraced comedian was jailed for rape and sexual assault.
Footage of Fielding and Brand joking about rape with TV presenter Jonathan Ross on an episode of Channel 4's Big Fat Quiz of the Year in 2007 has resurfaced in the aftermath of Brand's conviction.
Fielding described "some of the jokes" he made as "horrible and inappropriate", and said he had not been in contact with Brand "for many years".

articles.title: Ridley Scott's Blade Runner Used Extra Footage From A Stanley Kubrick Movie
articles.summary: One version of Blade Runner required a happier ending than director Ridley Scott originally intended, so he called fellow director Stanley Kubrick for help.
body: In the American theatrical version of Ridley Scott's 1982 sci-fi film "Blade Runner," the film had a happy ending for Rick and Rachael.

This was an alteration made to "Blade Runner" after Scott's original cut was not well-received by test audiences. Scott's intended ending involved a weirdly symbolic image of a character examining a piece of origami folded into a unicorn, and Rick Deckard (Harrison Ford) walking into an elevator with the replicant Rachael (Sean Young). The ending was ambiguous and downbeat, in the spirit of film noir.

Scott recalled the experience in a 2015 interview with The Hollywood Reporter, saying that an unnamed investor wanted him to tack on a happy ending where Rick and Rachel drive off into the woods together. In the happy ending, Rick talks in voiceover about how Rachel is a special kind of replicant who can live indefinitely. Harrison Ford is on record about how much he hates that voiceover.
There have been many cuts of "Blade Runner" over the years, and Scott has been very frank about how much he dislikes the "happy ending" that was mandated to him.
